entries.card: why:PLACED 2026-08-11. THE BLOCK IS DOCUMENTED AND THE LOT WITHI…
entries.text: PLACED 2026-08-11. THE BLOCK IS DOCUMENTED AND THE LOT WITHIN IT IS NOT. Andreas names the block face exactly — South Water Street between LaSalle and Wells — which is a 123 m frontage, about seven of the street's documented 55 ft lots. This record sits at the middle of it, which is a convention and not evidence. THE UNCERTAINTY IS ANISOTROPIC AND THE ALONG-STREET HALF IS THE BIG ONE: about 20 m across the street from the georeference (the datum data, 17.5 m RMS), and about 60 m along it, because the store could have stood at either end of the block face. THE SIDE OF THE STREET IS NOT ARBITRARY: the north side of South Water was the river bank, wharves and landings (the research notes on structures south § 12), and a purchased LOT with a store erected on it is a south-side lot. METHOD: the modern intersection centres either end of the block were read from OpenStreetMap at EPSG:26916 — West Upper Wacker Drive / North Wells E 447402.5, N 4637411.6 and West Upper Wacker Drive / North LaSalle E 447525.2, N 4637408.1, fetched 2026-08-11 — the street's centreline interpolated between them at the mid-block easting, the south kerb taken 12.2 m south of that as half an 80 ft platted street, and the footprint's north face set on it. South Water Street is today's Wacker Drive along the south bank, per this project's street-name key. A CHECK: the traced 1834 south bank of the main stem runs 41.7 m north of this record's north face at this easting, which is a plausible street plus wharf depth but is 23 m more than the same measurement at Dearborn — the difference is the georeference's local paper stretch and the uneven build-out of Wacker Drive over the old dock line, not a real widening of the river frontage. Facade bearing 0, north onto South Water, inferred from the street rather than from any statement. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-27, AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE — ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above set this footprint's north face on the South Water frontage, and it found that frontage by taking the MODERN West Wacker Drive centreline out of OpenStreetMap and stepping 12.2 m south of it. That is not this project's own South Water Street: the committed centreline in the 1835 streets data, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what the plat lots generator builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it, this record's north wall stood 6.62 m OUT PAST the block 19 frontage line, in the platted roadway — far enough into it that the frontage works generator refused the plank sidewalk along this stretch of South Water in writing and named this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 8.12 m along the face's inward normal — dE +0.067 m, dN -8.119 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447460.0 N 4637391.6 becomes E 447460.067 N 4637383.481 — which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line, the same margin the block infill generator gives every reconstructed unit standing on this face, and the same repair the six reconciled under other work carry. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade — re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence. WHY IT TOOK A SECOND RUN, AND WHOSE DECISION IT WAS. Other work measured this exact translation and REFUSED to apply it, for a reason that was real: reconciled onto the plat this building SEATS on lot 2 of block 19, and that lot is one the 665-roof schedule had already dealt to the anonymous South Water frontage run, which the block infill generator refused — one principal roof to a lot. Nothing overlapped; the worst overlap between any of the eleven South Water placements and any committed footprint in the town is zero. What refused this repair was a RULE about entitlement, not the ground. THE OWNER RULED ON 2026-08-27 that a platted business-front lot may carry a documented store at the street AND an anonymous dwelling behind it, on the reasoning that the geometry already permits it and the alternative pays eight roofs and two households for a rule the corrected data had itself called into question. The clause and its three tests are written into the plat occupancy tool; no roof left the town and no household moved. WHAT IS STILL WRONG AND IS LEFT WRITTEN DOWN: the facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 359.53 (i.e. -0.47), so the front wall is 1.50 m back at its worst corner and up to 1.56 m at the other. That skew is smaller than the walk's own daylight and it is not corrected here, because rotating a documented record is a second claim and this one is a repair.

levels.8-10: A paper names the block, but not the lot on it. A history book says South Water Street between LaSalle and Wells. That stretch is about 400 feet, about seven lots. We set the store in the middle of it. That is our habit, not proof. Our spot may be off by about 65 feet across the street, but by about 195 feet along it, since nothing says where on the block it stood. The north side of South Water Street was the river bank, with wharves. So a store goes on the south side. Where it sits across the street could be off by about 20 m. Our first spot for this building was measured from a modern street, not from our own street of 1835. Against our own street, its front wall stood 6.62 m out in the road, so the plank walk could not pass it. So we moved it back. What we claim about it did not change, only the line we measured from. We moved this building 8.12 m so its north wall stands 1.50 m back from the street line. Our other made-up buildings on this street stand the same way. Nothing moved along the street. Fixing a point with better lines is not new proof, so how sure we are stays the same. At first we did not make this move. On our plan the store would sit on a lot already given to a made-up house, and our rule allowed one main roof to a lot. On 27 August 2026 the owner of this project ruled that a shop lot may hold a real store at the street and a made-up home behind it. So the move was made, and no house or family left the town. One small thing is still off. The front is turned a tiny bit from the line of the street, so one corner sits a little farther back. We leave it, since turning a real building would be a new claim.

WHAT IS STILL WRONG AND IS LEFT WRITTEN DOWN: the facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 0.93, so the front wall is 1.50 m back at its worst corner and up to 1.65 m at the other. Measured against the committed plat with the corridor intrusion check, this footprint still laps Dearborn's corridor by 0.20 m — the third-shallowest lap any building in this town makes. WHY IT IS NOT REPAIRED, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES IT. the corridor intrusion check --escape bisects the shortest translation that takes each lapping record clear of the corridor it laps and reads that direction against the record's OWN facade bearing: here it is 0.202 m on a bearing of 270.36 degrees, which is 0.36 degrees off square to this facade — a slide SIDEWAYS ACROSS ITS OWN FRONT, not in or out of it. South Water's committed axis runs at 90.93 degrees beside this footprint, so that escape is a move ALONG South Water Street to within 0.6 of a degree. It would therefore change where along the business street this building stands, and the corner is the one part of this placement a source argues. Moving ACROSS the front is a different operation and is the one other work defended: the setback is re-derived against a better line and the claim does not move. Moving ALONG it moves the claim. PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED, so the tag follows the weaker half, which is the reading the Sauganash, the Green Tree and Peck's store all carry. METHOD, the project's standard one: Lake Street and Clark Street both survive on their 1830 plat lines, and the modern West Lake Street / North Clark Street intersection centre was read from OpenStreetMap at EPSG:26916 E 447649.73, N 4637283.43 (OSM node 258957339, fetched 2026-08-11). The footprint origin is set 12.2 m west and 12.2 m south of that centre less the building's own width and depth, so that the church's north face sits on the Lake Street frontage and its east face on the Clark Street frontage of a south-west corner lot. 12.2 m is half of an 80 ft street, the width annotated on Hathaway 1834; Currey has the 1830 Thompson plat laying streets out 'uniformly 66 feet wide', which would move each offset 2.1 m, and that discrepancy is already recorded in the research notes on hogan store section 5. WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M, which is the georeference's residual (the datum data: 17.5 m RMS on Wright 1834, with 3.7 per cent paper stretch), not an additional guess. A LARGER AND ONE-DIRECTIONAL ERROR SITS ON TOP OF IT, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH READING. The lot description carried by this project's dossier is 'the south 25 ft of Lot 1, Block 34', and the building is 25 ft in one dimension - so the church did not stand on the corner of its lot but filled the strip at the SOUTH end of it, set back from the Lake Street line by whatever the rest of Lot 1 measured. Nothing reached states the lot's depth. On an 80 x 150 ft platted lot the setback would be about 38 m; on a lot fronting Clark instead of Lake it would be nothing at all and the church would be 25 ft wide on Clark with its 40 ft dimension running back, which is a different building from the one modelled here. This record places the church ON the corner and states the direction of the likely error: if it is wrong it is wrong to the SOUTH, by up to about a lot depth. Facade bearing 0, due north onto Lake, INFERRED FROM THE 25 FT STRIP RATHER THAN FROM ANY STATEMENT about which way the church faced: a strip 25 ft deep measured north-south puts the 40 ft dimension east-west and the long elevation parallel to Lake Street. The slough that lay in front of the church at this corner, which the congregation crossed on planks and benches in the spring, is not modelled. REFUSED 2026-08-27, IN WRITING AND WITH THE NUMBERS THAT REFUSED IT. This record carries the same fault the three Lake Street placements reconciled beside it carried: the cross-street coordinate was taken off a MODERN kerb line read from OpenStreetMap rather than off this project's committed Lake Street centreline, and measured against the committed line this footprint's north wall stands 1.90 m OUT PAST the block 34 frontage line, in the platted roadway. the frontage works py's generator march refuses two steps of Lake Street's plank sidewalk for it — 88.6 to 99.0 m along that face — and names this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR WAS MEASURED AND REFUSED FOR A FORTNIGHT, AND THE NUMBER IS WHY: the same derivation the other three take translates this footprint 3.395 m along the face's inward normal, and a physicians office stood 3.15 m behind it on the same lot — block 34 lot 6, which also carries a privy and a one-and-a-half-story frame cottage. Moved 0.2 m the two were inside the 3.0 m the separation gate requires; moved 3.2 m they physically OVERLAPPED. There was no translation along this normal that both cleared the walk and left the pair standing apart, so WHAT WAS BEING ASKED WAS A RULE AND NOT A METRE: a physicians office is a product of the inferred-household programme, carrying reconstruction.status "inferred household" and standing 8.90 m back from the frontage line on the lot a documented church would come onto, and whether a documented building displaces an inferred household unit decides what this town's evidence layers owe each other. That went to the owner as other work with all three options measured.

THE OWNER RULED ON 2026-09-21 AND THE RULE IS GENERAL: where an ATTESTED placement and an INFERRED placement collide on one lot, the attested one stands and the inferred one moves or is withdrawn. "A building the sources put on a street is the kind of thing this project exists to hold; a unit the reconstruction placed is a best guess, and a best guess that displaces a document has the method backwards." He refused the third option in terms — narrowing the two footprints to make 3.395 m and 3.15 m fit would leave two buildings sized to each other rather than to their evidence — and left what happens to the office to the run, re-seating before withdrawal. RECONCILED HERE ON THAT RULING, 2026-09-26, BY THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 3.395 m along the face's inward normal — dE -0.028 m, dN -3.395 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447625.34 N 4637263.61 becomes E 447625.312 N 4637260.215 — which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line, the same margin the block infill generator gives every reconstructed unit on this face and the same one The Old Bank Building, George W. Dole's Warehouse and St. Mary's Catholic Church took under other work. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade — re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence, and every uncertainty stated above still stands at its stated size, including the one-directional lot-depth error toward the south. WHAT MOVED INSTEAD WAS a physicians office, which vacated the ground and was RE-SEATED rather than withdrawn: it keeps its Lake Street frontage band, its face and this same lot 6, 12.99 m west along the face and forward onto the street line, which is its own C1 clause's answer. Its card carries the rule and the numbers that displaced it. Measured after both moves, the nearest committed footprint to this one is a physicians office at 3.101 m, clear of the 3.0 m the separation gate requires, the next is a one-and-a-half-story frame cottage at 7.78 m, and no committed footprint in the town overlaps this one by a square centimetre. THE SEPARATION GATE WAS NOT WEAKENED AND NEITHER FOOTPRINT WAS NARROWED. The two steps of Lake Street's plank walk this record refused — 88.6 to 99.0 m along block 34's north face — are laid by the frontage works py's generator own march now that the wall is off the roadway; nothing in that generator was relaxed to lay them. MOVED BACK ONTO ITS LOT 2026-11-03, on the owner's report of buildings 'placed in the middle of the walkways or alleys': its side wall stood 1.91 m out past the Clark Street lot line of block 34, on the plank walk's line; moved 2.41 m back so that wall stands 0.50 m inside the lot line. The translation is dE -2.41 m, dN +0.02 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447625.312 N 4637260.215 becomes E 447622.899 N 4637260.23. NOTHING THE SOURCES SAY MOVED: the corner, side, block or cluster this record is placed by is unchanged, and so is its confidence grade; the coordinate was derived, never read, so it is re-derived against this project's own platted lot line and alley, which the structure clearance check now holds every 1835 building to.

levels.8-10: We placed it in August 2026. A paper names its corner, but our spot on it is worked out, so we count it as a good guess. Lake Street and Clark Street still run where the 1830 plan put them. We read their crossing from a modern map, then moved in half a street's width each way, to the south west corner. Another book's street width would move it a little. Our spot may be off by about 65 feet, the error of the old map. A bigger error sits on top of that, and it goes one way. The land paper says the church stood on the south 25 feet of Lot 1, and the church is 25 feet across one way. So the church did not stand on the corner of its lot. It filled the strip at the south end, back from Lake Street. No paper gives the lot's depth. On a usual lot it would stand about 125 feet back. If the lot faced Clark instead, it would be a different building from ours. We put it on the corner, and say that if we are wrong, it is too far north. Its long side faces Lake Street, from the shape of that strip. In spring a swamp lay in front of the church, crossed on planks and benches. We do not draw it. We said no to a fix in August 2026, in writing and with the numbers. This church had the same fault as three other buildings on Lake Street. Its spot was measured from a modern street, not from our own Lake Street line. Against our line, its front wall stood about six feet out in the road. Our plank walk then could not be laid in front of it. We measured the fix and held off for two weeks, and the number shows why. Moving the church back the right amount would push it into a doctor's office behind it on the same lot. Moved a little, the two were too close. Moved enough, they overlapped. No move did both. So the real question was a rule. That office is one of our made up homes, a best guess, while the church is in the papers. We asked the owner of this project. In September 2026 he ruled: where a building from the papers and a made up building meet on one lot, the one from the papers stands, and the made up one moves or goes. A best guess that pushes out a paper has the method backwards. He said no to making both buildings narrower. We fixed it on that ruling in September 2026. We used its own method, run against our own street line. We moved the church about eleven feet back. Now its front wall stands about five feet behind the street line. Every made up building on this street gets the same gap. Three other buildings got the same fix. Nothing moved along the street. Fixing a point with better lines is not new proof, so how sure we are stays the same. We did not loosen the gap rule, and we did not make either building narrower. The plank walk is now laid in front of the church as usual. In November 2026 the owner of this project reported buildings standing in walkways and alleys. This church's side wall stuck out onto the Clark Street walk. So we moved it about eight feet back onto its lot. Nothing the papers say has moved. The corner, side or block we place it by is the same, and so is how sure we are. entries.text: PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED, so the tag follows the weaker half. Andreas puts the log jail on 'the northwest corner of the court-house square'. The public square is the block bounded by Randolph Street on the north, Washington Street on the south, Clark Street on the east and LaSalle Street on the west - the block this project's own ground control identifies as such in the wright 1834 gcps data, where LaSalle and Randolph is labelled 'NW corner of the Public Square block' and Clark and Washington 'SE corner of the Public Square block'. Its four inside corners were computed for this parcel from modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres fetched 2026-08-11, offset 12.2 m into the block on each axis, half of an 80 ft street per Hathaway 1834: NW 447538.25 / 4637130.78, NE 447639.27 / 4637130.25, SW 447541.20 / 4637018.49, SE 447639.80 / 4637018.05, which makes the block about 101 x 112 m. The jail's own north-west corner is set on the square's north-west corner, so the footprint origin - which is the building's south-west corner - sits its own depth south of it. THIS IS A CORNER OF A BLOCK, NOT A LOT, so it is a weaker statement than the corner-lot placements elsewhere in this dataset: nothing says how far into the block the building stood, whether it was set back from either street line, or which way it faced. WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M from the georeference (the datum data: 17.5 m RMS on Wright 1834, 3.7 per cent paper stretch), plus an unquantified setback into the block. Facade bearing 0, due north onto Randolph, CONVENTION RATHER THAN EVIDENCE - a jail at the north-west corner could as reasonably have faced west onto LaSalle or inward onto the square, and nothing attests it. The square itself in 1835 was otherwise an open, unimproved prairie block, fenced or not; no fence, path or improvement of the block is modelled. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-28, AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE - ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above found the square's north-west corner by taking modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres, fetched 2026-08-11, and stepping 12.2 m into the block on each axis. That is not this project's own Randolph Street: the committed centreline in the 1835 streets data, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what the plat lots generator builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it with the corridor intrusion check, this footprint's north wall stood 3.48 m OUT PAST block 39's Randolph frontage line, in the platted roadway, with its centroid inside the corridor - deeper than any of the four Lake Street records other work looked at - and the frontage works generator refused two steps of Randolph's plank walk, 0.0 to 10.4 m along that face, naming this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 4.981 m along the face's inward normal - dE -0.040 m, dN -4.981 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447538.25 N 4637126.21 becomes E 447538.21 N 4637121.23 - which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line. THE SQUARE IS NOT SUBDIVIDED, so there is no lot line to stand off: 1.50 m is plat occupancy lot margin m, the plat module's own margin off a boundary, and it is the same figure the reconciled South Water and Lake records took off their lot lines. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade - re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence, and Andreas's 'northwest corner of the court-house square' is what it always was. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REPAIR: the 20 m working uncertainty stated above is unchanged and dwarfs this 4.98 m, so the move is a reconciliation between two of this project's own lines and not a claim to have located the jail better. entries.text: PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED TWICE AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED, so the tag follows the weaker half — the rule the Sauganash and Green Tree placements use. Wau-Bun: 'It stood at what is now the southwest corner of Wolcott and N. Water Streets.' Andreas, independently: 'the agency-house on the north side of the river, near where now is the foot of North State Street', with his footnote citing Wau-Bun for the same corner. METHOD, in three steps. (1) Wolcott Street is today's N State Street; its modern centreline was read from OpenStreetMap through the Kinzie intersection (EPSG:26916 E 447899.73, N 4637671.53, local E +827.0, N +275.7) and carried south on the fitted bearing of the OSM centreline, giving E +830 at this northing and a west kerb 12.2 m west of it, half an 80 ft platted street. (2) North Water Street and the 1834 north bank were read off the Wright 1834 sheet at the project's own fitted affine (the wright (px) tool, the same transform the rederive datum tool checks the datum against): the north-bank block row's south line, which is North Water Street's north kerb, runs at local N +128 to +132 between E +624 and E +812, and the drawn north bank of the main stem runs at local N +98 over the same stretch. So the platted street occupies a strip about 30 m deep between the block row and the water. (3) The building's south face is set 15 m north of that bank line and its east face 4 m west of the State Street kerb. THE 15 M IS EVIDENCE, NOT A GUESS, AND IT IS SOFT: Andreas prints the testimony of Charles Jouett's daughter, Mrs. Susan M. Callis, who came here in 1816 and describes the agency house of that period as 'a log building of two large rooms, about twenty steps from the river bank, on the north side'. Twenty steps is 15-18 m. Two inferences ride on it — that a step is about three-quarters of a metre, and that the house Mrs. Callis describes is the one Wolcott finished, which Andreas's 'commenced during Judge Jouett's incumbency' supports and nobody states. WHAT THE SOUTH-WEST QUADRANT ACTUALLY IS: on the 1834 sheet there is no block in it. West of Wolcott the ground south of North Water Street is the riverbank itself, so the building sits on the bank between the platted street and the water rather than on a corner lot — which is what Wau-Bun describes from the other side: 'when, in the process of the town's improvement, a street was maliciously opened directly in the rear of the building, the whole establishment, with its comical little adjuncts, was a constant source of amusement to the passers-by.' The house predates the plat by a decade and the street was laid out behind it. That same sentence is the evidence for the facade bearing recorded here, 180, due south onto the river: the street opened at the REAR, so the front faced the water, which is also how the fort's people reached it — Wau-Bun has the intercourse between the garrison and the Agency House kept up by canoe. UNCERTAINTY: about 20 m from the georeference (the datum data records ~17.5 m RMS and calls 20 m the working figure), plus the reading of the 1834 sheet by eye at about 5 m, plus whatever 'twenty steps' is worth. Treat the across-bank axis as the softer one. A LARGER CAVEAT THAN ALL OF THOSE, AND IT IS DISCHARGED. When this note was written the building stood about 500 m east of the modelled terrain box and there was no modelled ground under it at all. The the 1834 harbor cut ground heightfield was extended east on 2026-08-11 to local E -320..+1700, N -400..+400 — the liberties register “Terrain: the ground continues past the modelled box as a radial skirt” is revised to say so — and this position has stood on traced ground at about +1.35 m above the summer-1835 water surface ever since, which is why this phase carries no ground contact declaration. Corrected 2026-08-22 under other work; walked in the real page by the east band check.

levels.8-10: We placed it in August 2026. A paper names its corner, the south west corner of Wolcott and N. Water Streets. But our spot on that corner is worked out, so we count it as a good guess. We read the street crossing from a modern map, then moved in half a street's width each way. Our spot may be off by about 65 feet, the error of the old map. The distance of about 50 feet is from a paper, not a guess, but it is loose. A history book prints what Charles Jouett's daughter, Mrs Susan Callis, said. She came here in 1816. She said the agency house was a log building of two large rooms, about twenty steps from the river bank, on the north side. Twenty steps is about 50 to 60 feet. Two guesses ride on that: how long a step is, and that the house she saw is the one Wolcott finished. A history book's words back up the second, but no one says it. The corner here is not really a corner lot. On the 1834 map there is no block there. The ground south of North Water Street is the river bank itself. So the house sits on the bank between the street and the water. A book of 1831 describes it from the other side. It says a street was opened right behind the building, so passers by could laugh at the whole place and its little sheds. The house is ten years older than the town plan, and the street was laid out behind it. That same line tells us which way it faced. The street ran at the back, so the front faced south, onto the river. The fort's people came to it by canoe. Our spot may be off by about 65 feet, from the old map. Reading the map by eye adds a little. And twenty steps is a loose measure. The distance from the bank is the looser one. A bigger worry than all of those has now gone away. When we wrote this, the building stood far east of our ground, with no ground under it at all. In August 2026 we grew our ground east. Since then the house has stood on traced ground, a little above the summer water of 1835. So it needs no special note.

entries.card: why:PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED TWICE IN ANDREAS…
entries.text:
PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED TWICE IN ANDREAS, IN TWO DIFFERENT CHAPTERS, AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED - so the tag follows the weaker half. 'a new house on the northwest corner of Wells and Lake streets' (hotel chapter) and 'another house on the northwest corner of Wells and Lake streets' (life of Mark Beaubien). "A Chronology of Early Chicago Area Hotels." Digital Research Library of… agrees. METHOD, the project's standard one: Lake Street and Wells Street both survive on their 1830 plat lines, and the modern West Lake Street / North Wells Street intersection centre was read from OpenStreetMap at EPSG:26916 E 447404.02, N 4637283.94 (OSM node 258957316, fetched 2026-08-11). The building's south face is set on the Lake Street frontage 12.2 m north of that centre and its east face on the Wells frontage 12.2 m west of it, 12.2 m being half of an 80 ft street as annotated on Hathaway 1834; the stored coordinate is the polygon origin AFTER the 180 degree facade bearing, which under the renderer's convention (the walkthrough's walker code) puts it at the building's north-east corner. Currey has the 1830 Thompson plat laying streets 'uniformly 66 feet wide', which would move each offset 2.1 m - the discrepancy recorded in the research notes on hogan store section 5. WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M, which is the georeference's residual (the datum data: 17.5 m RMS on Wright 1834), not an additional guess. Facade bearing 180, due south onto Lake Street. THAT BEARING IS THE WEAKEST THING HERE: no source says which street the house fronted, and a corner house whose name is an EXCHANGE and whose office booked stage seats could as well have turned its front to Wells. Lake is chosen because it was one of the town's two principal thoroughfares and because the building's neighbours on this record's own street line - the Green Tree three blocks west, the Sauganash two blocks west - front their long side to Lake. THE GROUND UNDER IT IS MODELLED and the building lands on it within the walker's 0.35 m step-up rule, so the phase carries no ground contact declaration. Note that this footprint would have sat exactly on the OLD box edge - local E +305.1 to +319.1 against an edge at +320 - and that the the 1834 harbor cut ground heightfield has since been extended to E +1700, which is what puts real terrain under the rest of this parcel too.

THE CORNER IS RULED, 2026-09-26, AND THIS POSITION DOES NOT MOVE. Other work recorded a conflict on this record the day before — that Russell E. Heacock's advertisement puts this house one block west, at Lake and Franklin — and the conflict does not survive being read against the claim it came from. The advertisement is the Chicago Democrat of 1835-07-08, and what it places is HEACOCK'S OWN OFFICE and not this building: '[Office in the 2d st]ory, opposite the Ex[cha]n[ge], [corne]r of Lake and Franklin-sts.' The corner clause is the advertiser's address — the one thing a notice like this exists to give — and the Exchange stands in it as the landmark opposite. NOTE ALSO WHAT THE PAPER PRINTS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: the surviving type reads 'the Ex[cha]n[ge]', not 'the Exchange Coffee House'; the longer form was the reader's expansion, and the note other work wrote quoted the expansion back as though it were the page. THIS PROJECT'S OWN REGISTER ALREADY READ IT THE RULED WAY, which is what settles it: the claim's `business.placement` records `class: corner` with `anchor: 'the Exchange'`, and the biz russell e heacock data carries one anchored location at the franklin+lake crossing with structure id: null and the register's action: new building — Heacock at that corner, in no roof this town holds. So the disagreement was between two READINGS of one advertisement, not between two sources about one building, and Andreas's north-west corner of Wells and Lake — twice, in two chapters, with "A Chronology of Early Chicago Area Hotels." Digital Research Library of… agreeing — is unopposed. WHAT THE RULING COSTS, STATED RATHER THAN TIDIED: 'opposite' must then reach from the Franklin corner to this house, about one block of Lake Street. It reaches if Heacock's second story stood on the SOUTH side of Lake at Franklin, because the block face across Lake from there runs Franklin to Wells and this house holds its east end; it does not reach if he stood on the north side, and then 'opposite' is the loose usage for the way across the street. Nothing in the notice says which side he was on and nothing here chooses — both readings leave this corner where Andreas put it, which is why the residual does not touch the coordinate. THE TAG IS UNCHANGED AT `inferred` AND THE SOURCE LIST IS UNCHANGED: the ruling removes an objection and adds no witness to the coordinate, which is still derived from a modern intersection centre. The advertisement is evidence about Heacock's office, and it is cited on that record. MOVED BACK ONTO ITS LOT 2026-11-03, on the owner's report of buildings 'placed in the middle of the walkways or alleys': its side wall stood 1.44 m out past the Wells Street lot line of block 20, on the plank walk's line; moved 1.54 m back so that wall stands 0.10 m inside the lot line. The translation is dE -1.54 m, dN +0.01 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447391.82 N 4637305.14 becomes E 447390.282 N 4637305.149. NOTHING THE SOURCES SAY MOVED: the corner, side, block or cluster this record is placed by is unchanged, and so is its confidence grade; the coordinate was derived, never read, so it is re-derived against this project's own platted lot line and alley, which the structure clearance check now holds every 1835 building to. Its side wall is held 0.10 m inside the lot line rather than 0.50 m: the New York House stands against its west wall, and half a metre more would put the two 0.47 m into each other, past the 0.40 m party wall the structure clearance check allows.

levels.8-10: We placed it in August 2026. A paper names its corner, the north west corner of Wells and Lake Streets. But our spot on that corner is worked out, so we count it as a good guess. We read the street crossing from a modern map, then moved in half a street's width each way. Our spot may be off by about 65 feet, the error of the old map. Which way it faced is the weakest thing here. No paper says which street the house fronted. It was a corner house called an Exchange, where stage seats were sold. It could as well have faced Wells Street. We chose Lake Street, one of the town's two main streets. Its neighbours here face their long side to Lake too. In September 2026 we ruled on its corner, and it did not move. Someone had found an ad by Russell Heacock. It seemed to put this house a block west, at Lake and Franklin. But the ad places Heacock's own office, not this house. It says his office was upstairs, opposite the Exchange, at the corner of Lake and Franklin. The corner is his address. The Exchange is just the landmark across from it. Look too at what the paper prints and what it does not. The type that is left says the Exchange. It does not say the Exchange Coffee House. The longer name was a reader's guess. Then it was quoted as if it were the page. Our own records had already read it the right way. They put Heacock at that corner, in a building we do not hold. So the question was two readings of one ad. It was not two papers about one building. The history book puts this house on the north west corner of Wells and Lake, twice. Another list agrees. Nothing now goes against that. Here is what the ruling costs, said plainly. Opposite must reach from the Franklin corner to this house. That is about one block along Lake Street. It reaches if Heacock's office stood on the south side of Lake. It does not if he stood on the north side. Then opposite just means across the way. Nothing says which side he was on, and we do not choose. Either way the house stays where the history book put it. How sure we are does not change, and no paper is added. In November 2026 the owner of this project reported buildings standing in walkways and alleys. This one's side wall stuck out onto the Wells Street walk. So we moved it about five feet back onto its lot. Nothing the papers say has moved. The corner, side or block we place it by is the same, and so is how sure we are. We only worked out its spot again against our own lot lines and alleys, which every 1835 building must now keep clear of.

entries.text: PLACED 2026-08-11. THE JUNCTION AND THE CORNER ARE NOT THE SAME CLAIM HERE AND THEY DO NOT REST ON THE SAME EVIDENCE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS NOTE. The JUNCTION is documented by the paper itself: the imprint of the first issue, 26 November 1833, reads 'in the building on the corner of South Water and Clark-streets'. That is a contemporary self-reported address, and it is the strongest positional evidence any structure record in this dataset carries. The CORNER — which of the four — is NOT in the imprint, which says only 'on the corner of'. It comes from Andreas, writing fifty years later: 'An office was secured in a building on the southwest corner of South Water and Clark streets, which was unfinished at the time.' This project grades Andreas gathered from witnesses, a pioneer recollection compiled half a century after the fact, and the corner therefore stays INFERRED while the junction would stand on its own. Two of the four corners can be set aside independently: the north side of South Water at Clark was the river frontage, wharves and landings (the research notes on structures south § 12), so the choice is between the south-west and the south-east, and Andreas's south-west is the only statement either way. METHOD: the modern West Upper Wacker Drive / North Clark Street intersection centre was read from OpenStreetMap at EPSG:26916 E 447648.5, N 4637409.7 (two nodes averaged, spread 14.3 m, fetched 2026-08-11); the footprint origin sits 12.2 m west and 12.2 m south of it less the building's own width and depth, so the north face is on the South Water frontage and the east face on the Clark frontage of a south-west corner lot. South Water Street is today's Wacker Drive along the south bank, per this project's street-name key (the research notes on structures north). WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M from the georeference (the datum data, 17.5 m RMS), plus about 37 m if the corner is wrong — that is the distance from here to the south-east corner, where Harmon & Loomis's Store is recorded. LOCAL WARP WORTH RECORDING: this project's traced 1834 south bank runs 77.5 m north of this record's north face at this easting, against 41.6 m at LaSalle and 18.7 m at Dearborn. A 60 m swing across four blocks is not a real riverbank shape; it is the georeference's local paper stretch plus Wacker Drive having been built out over the old dock line by different amounts along its length. Do not read the gap as wharf depth. Facade bearing 0, due north onto South Water, inferred from the street rather than from any statement. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-24, AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE — ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above set this footprint's north face on the South Water frontage, and it found that frontage by taking the MODERN West Wacker Drive centreline out of OpenStreetMap and stepping 12.2 m south of it. That is not this project's own South Water Street: the committed centreline in the 1835 streets data, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what the plat lots generator builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it, this record's north wall stood 5.11 m OUT PAST the block 18 frontage line, in the platted roadway — far enough into it that the frontage works generator refused the plank sidewalk along this stretch of South Water in writing and named this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 6.61 m along the face's inward normal — dE +0.053 m, dN -6.609 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447624.1 N 4637389.9 becomes E 447624.153 N 4637383.291 — which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line, the same margin the block infill generator gives every reconstructed unit standing on this face. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade — re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence. WHAT IS STILL WRONG AND IS LEFT WRITTEN DOWN: the facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 359.538 (i.e. -0.462), so the front wall is 1.50 m back at its worst corner and up to 1.60 m at the other. That skew is smaller than the walk's own daylight and it is not corrected here, because rotating a documented record is a second claim and this one is a repair.

levels.8-10: The crossing and the corner are two different claims, resting on different proof. That is the point of this note. The crossing is in the paper itself. Its first issue, of 26 November 1833, says it is in the building on the corner of South Water and Clark Streets. That is an address in the paper's own words, the strongest proof of place any building here has. But it does not say which of the four corners. That comes from a history book written fifty years later, which says the south west corner, in a building not yet finished. So the corner stays a good guess. The north side of the street was the river front, with wharves. That leaves south west or south east, and the book says south west. If it is wrong, it belongs about 120 feet east. A local stretch worth writing down. The river bank we traced from the 1834 map runs about 255 feet north of this office, but much closer at the next two streets. A river bank does not really swing like that. It is the old map's stretch, and the modern street built out over the old docks by different amounts. Do not read the gap as wharf depth. Its front faces north onto South Water Street, from the street, not from any paper. Our first spot for this building was measured from a modern street, not from our own street of 1835. Against our own street, its front wall stood 5.11 m out in the road, so the plank walk could not pass it. So we moved it back. What we claim about it did not change, only the line we measured from. We moved this building 6.61 m so its north wall stands 1.50 m back from the street line. Our other made-up buildings on this street stand the same way. Nothing moved along the street. Fixing a point with better lines is not new proof, so how sure we are stays the same. One small thing is still off. The front is turned a tiny bit from the line of the street, so one corner sits a little farther back. We leave it, since turning a real building would be a new claim.

entries.text: PLACED 2026-08-11. THE JUNCTION IS ATTESTED AND THE CORNER IS THIS RECORD'S CHOICE, ARGUED HERE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Andreas gives 'corner of Clark and South Water' and never a side. Two of the four corners fall away on the dossier's own evidence: the north side of South Water was the river frontage, wharves and landings (the research notes on structures south § 12), so the building is south of the street. That leaves south-west and south-east. THE SOUTH-WEST IS SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY CLAIMED: Andreas puts the Chicago Democrat's building on the south-west corner of the same junction, and the Democrat's own first issue confirms the junction from a contemporary imprint. This record therefore takes the south-east, and the reasoning is that two attested premises on one crossing are better modelled as two buildings on two corners than as one building asserted twice — but that is a modelling choice, not evidence, AND THE HONEST ALTERNATIVE IS THAT THEY WERE ONE BUILDING. Andreas says Calhoun 'secured an office IN a building' at this junction, i.e. he rented; Harmon & Loomis owned a building at this junction; a newspaper renting an office in a merchant's corner store is the ordinary arrangement of the period. IF THAT IS RIGHT, THIS RECORD STANDS ABOUT 37 M EAST OF WHERE IT BELONGS AND DUPLICATES The Chicago Democrat Office. That is recorded here, in that record, and in both research docs rather than being resolved by preference. METHOD: the modern West Upper Wacker Drive / North Clark Street intersection centre was read from OpenStreetMap at EPSG:26916 E 447648.5, N 4637409.7 (two nodes averaged, spread 14.3 m, fetched 2026-08-11); the origin sits 12.2 m east and 12.2 m south of it less the depth, so the north face is on the South Water frontage and the west face on the Clark frontage of a south-east corner lot. The traced 1834 south bank runs 79.6 m north of this north face at this easting, which is 60 m more than the same measurement at Dearborn — local paper stretch and Wacker Drive's uneven build-out over the old dock line, not wharf depth. Facade bearing 0, north onto South Water, inferred from the street rather than from any statement. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-24, AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE — ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above set this footprint's north face on the South Water frontage, and it found that frontage by taking the MODERN West Wacker Drive centreline out of OpenStreetMap and stepping 12.2 m south of it. That is not this project's own South Water Street: the committed centreline in the 1835 streets data, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what the plat lots generator builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it, this record's north wall stood 5.30 m OUT PAST the block 17 frontage line, in the platted roadway — far enough into it that the frontage works generator refused the plank sidewalk along this stretch of South Water in writing and named this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 6.80 m along the face's inward normal — dE -0.110 m, dN -6.805 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447660.7 N 4637389.9 becomes E 447660.59 N 4637383.095 — which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line, the same margin the block infill generator gives every reconstructed unit standing on this face. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade — re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence. WHAT IS STILL WRONG AND IS LEFT WRITTEN DOWN: the facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 0.93, so the front wall is 1.50 m back at its worst corner and up to 1.70 m at the other. That skew is smaller than the walk's own daylight and it is not corrected here, because rotating a documented record is a second claim and this one is a repair. THE CROSS STREET IS REFUSED, IN WRITING, WITH THE NUMBER. The repair above answered South Water Street and could not answer this one, because a corner has two streets and the move that reconciles the frontage is along the other street's normal. Measured against the committed plat with the corridor intrusion check, this footprint still laps Clark's corridor by 0.21 m — the fourth-shallowest lap any building in this town makes, and the deepest of the three corner residuals the South Water repair left standing. It would therefore change where along the business street this building stands, and the corner is the one part of this placement a source argues. Moving ACROSS the front is a different operation and is the one other work defended: the setback is re-derived against a better line and the claim does not move. Moving ALONG it moves the claim. WHERE THE 0.2 M ACTUALLY COMES FROM, because it is not a mystery and should not be left as one. The method above stepped 12.2 m from an OpenStreetMap junction centre in BOTH directions. The South Water half of that offset was re-derived against this project's own committed centreline; the Clark half never was. levels.8-10: A paper names the crossing, but the corner is our choice, and we argue it here. A history book says the corner of Clark and South Water, and never a side. Two corners fall away. Against our own street, its front wall stood 5.30 m out in the road, so the plank walk could not pass it. So we moved it back. What we claim about it did not change, only the line we measured from. Fixing a point with better lines is not new proof, so how sure we are stays the same. One small thing is still off. We did not fix one small overlap, and we write down its size. This corner building sticks into Clark Street's space by about 8 inches. Fixing it would slide the building along the shop street. Its corner is the one part of its spot a paper gives. So moving it that way would change what we claim, and we leave it. The overlap comes from a tiny gap between a modern map and our own street line at this corner, and nothing else. It is about one hundredth of how far off our spot may be anyway.
